tip: When "vad" is the subject of the clause that follows, add "som": vad som kan hända (what can happen), not vad kan hända.
In a main clause a short adverb sits between "har" and the participle: har ofta besökt, not har besökt ofta.
For reaching an age, Swedish uses "fylla" (to fill): hon har fyllt tjugo = she has turned twenty.
"Slå sig ner" means to sit down or settle in; the reflexive is required: vi hade slagit oss ner.
The -s ending makes a passive with no helper verb: barnbidraget betalas ut = the allowance is paid out.
For food and drink pairings "till" means "to go with": en kanelbulle till kaffet, a bun with the coffee.
A length of time before a noun takes the genitive -s: fem veckors semester = five weeks of vacation.
Swedish builds the perfect with "har" even for motion verbs: jag har kommit hem, never "är kommit".
When a time phrase opens the sentence, the verb stays second, before the subject: den trettonde december firar vi.
